_comment: AWS's P-EAGLE drafters (arXiv 2602.01469): EAGLE-3 trained to draft every token of a step in one forward, its rows past the newest reading learned placeholders (the `ptd_token_id` token's embedding and `mask_hidden`, which vLLM's `parallel_drafting` loads the same way). It ships as its own checkpoint with its own config, whose `architectures` reads `LlamaForCausalLM`, so it names its target config (`head_targets`). It drafts only when `--speculative-model` names a checkpoint of it (`spec/mtp` compiles it): no published drafter of it beats its target alone on a base M5 yet (gpt-oss-20b at MLX 4-bit, one request: 57 tok/s alone; 42 drafting with AWS's bf16 drafter, which reads 1.4 GB a pass; 54.5 with its `-mixed` conversion — MLPs and `fc` at 4 bits, attention and embedding at 8 — at 2.38-2.46 tokens a step). Its tensors sit at the file's top level (`decoder_safetensors_prefix` empty): its first layer as `midlayer.*`, the rest as `layers.<L>.*`. The `-mixed` stem is that conversion: a 4-bit embedding loses most of the mask rows' acceptance (an MLX transcription of vLLM's drafter: 2.30 -> 1.80 tokens a step), the mix none. It borrows only its target's lm_head (`borrows`): AWS froze it in training, so the drafter's own copy is the target's bit for bit; its embedding it trained, so that one is its own. It drafts over its target vocabulary's first 65536 ids (`vocab_size`, the lm_head rows it reads), as Qwen3.5's head does; its embedding keeps every id (`embed_vocab_size`), the mask token's (201020) among them. `target_hidden_size` is the width of the three target hidden states `fc` fuses.
